1.1: The parables of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel;
1.2: to know wisdom and knowing; to understand the words of prudence;
1.3: and to take the learning of teach-ing; to take rightfulness [[or rightwise-ness]], and doom, and equity;
1.4: that fellness, or wariness, be given to little children, and knowing and understanding to a young waxing man.
1.5: A wise man hearing shall be the wiser; and a man understanding shall hold governance.
1.6: He shall perceive a parable, and the expounding; the words of wise men, and the dark figurative speeches of them.
1.7: The dread of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; fools despise wisdom and teaching.
1.8: My son, hear thou the teaching of thy father, and forsake thou not the law of thy mother;
1.9: that grace be added, either increased, to thine head, and a bie to thy neck.
1.10: My son, if sinners flatter thee, assent thou not to them.
1.11: If they say, Come thou with us, set we ambush to shed blood, hide we snares of deceits against an innocent without cause;
1.12: swallow we him, as hell swallow-eth a man living; and all-whole, as going down into a pit;
1.13: we shall find all precious chattel [[or substance]], we shall fill our houses with spoils;
1.14: put thou lot with us, one purse be there of us all;
1.15: my son, go thou not with them; forbid thy foot from the paths of them.
1.16: For the feet of them run to evil; and they hasten to shed out blood.
1.17: But a net is laid in vain before the eyes of birds, that have wings.
1.18: Also they set ambush against their own blood; and make ready frauds, or guiles, against their own souls.
1.19: So the paths of each avaricious man ravish, or take away, the souls of them that wield.
1.20: Wisdom preacheth withoutforth; in streets it giveth his voice.
1.21: It crieth oft in the head of companies; in the leaves of [[the]] gates of the city it bringeth forth his words, and saith,
1.22: How long, little men in wit, love young childhood, and fools shall covet those things, that be harmful to themselves, and unprudent men shall hate knowing?
1.23: Be ye converted at my reproving; lo, I shall bring forth to you my spirit, and I shall show my words.
1.24: For I called, and ye forsook; I held forth mine hand, and none there was that beheld.
1.25: Ye have despised all my counsel; and charged not my blamings.
1.26: And I shall laugh in your perishing; and I shall scorn you, when that, that ye dread, cometh to you.
1.27: When sudden wretchedness falleth in, and perishing befalleth as tempest; when tribulation and anguish cometh on you.
1.28: Then they shall call me, and I shall not hear; they shall rise early, and they shall not find me.
1.29: For they hated teaching, and they took not the dread of the Lord,
1.30: neither they assented to my counsel, and they depraved all mine amending.
1.31: Therefore they shall eat the fruits of their way; and they shall be filled with their counsels.
1.32: The turning away of little men in wit shall slay them; and the prosperity of fools shall lose them.
1.33: But he that heareth me, shall rest without dread; and he shall use abundance, when the dread of evils is taken away.

2.1: My son, if thou receivest my words, and hidest my behests with thee;
2.2: that thine ear hear wisdom, bow thine heart to know prudence.
2.3: For if thou inwardly callest wisdom, and bowest thine heart to prudence;
2.4: if thou seekest it as money, and diggest it out as treasures;
2.5: then thou shalt understand the dread of the Lord, and shalt find the knowing of God.
2.6: For the Lord giveth wisdom; and prudence and knowing is of his mouth.
2.7: He shall keep the health of rightful [[or rightwise]] men, and he shall defend them that go simply.
2.8: And he shall keep the paths of rightwiseness, and he shall keep the ways of holy men.
2.9: Then thou shalt understand rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]], and doom, and equity, and each good path.
2.10: If wisdom entereth into thine heart, and knowing pleaseth thy soul,
2.11: good counsel shall keep thee, and prudence shall keep thee;
2.12: that thou be delivered from an evil way, and from a man that speaketh wayward things.
2.13: Which forsake a rightful [[or right]] way, and go by dark ways;
2.14: which be glad, when they have done evil, and make full out joy in worst things;
2.15: whose ways be wayward, and their goings be of evil fame.
2.16: That thou be delivered from an alien woman, and from a strange woman, that maketh soft her words;
2.17: and forsaketh the duke of her time of marriage, and hath forgotten the covenant of her God.
2.18: For the house of her is bowed to death, and her paths to hell.
2.19: All that enter to her, shall not turn again, neither they shall catch the paths of life.
2.20: That thou go in a good way, and keep the paths of just [[or rightwise]] men.
2.21: Forsooth they that be rightful, shall dwell in the land; and simple men shall perfectly dwell therein.
2.22: But unfaithful men shall be lost from the land; and they that do wickedly, shall be taken away from it.

3.1: My son, forget thou not my law; and thine heart keep my command-ments.
3.2: For they shall set to thee the length of days, and the years of life, and peace.
3.3: Mercy and truth forsake thee not; bind thou those to thy throat, and write them in the tables of thine heart.
3.4: And thou shalt find grace, and good teaching before God and men.
3.5: Have thou trust in the Lord, of all thine heart; and lean thou not to thy prudence.
3.6: In all thy ways think on him, and he shall dress thy goings.
3.7: Be thou not wise with thyself; dread thou God, and go away from evil.
3.8: For why health shall be in thy navel, and moisting of thy bones.
3.9: Honour thou the Lord of thy chattel [[or substance]], and of the best of all thy fruits give thou to poor men;
3.10: and thy barns shall be filled with abundance, and thy pressers [[or presses]] shall flow with wine.
3.11: My son, cast thou not away the teaching of the Lord; and fail thou not, when thou art chastised of him.
3.12: For the Lord chastiseth him, whom he loveth; and as a father in the son he pleaseth him.
3.13: Blessed is the man that findeth wisdom, and that floweth with prudence.
3.14: The getting thereof is better than the merchandise [[or chaffering]] of gold and of silver; the fruits thereof be the first and the cleanest.
3.15: It is more precious than all riches; and all things that be desired, may not be comparisoned to this.
3.16: Length of days is in the right half thereof, and riches and glory be in the left half thereof.
3.17: The ways thereof be fair ways, and all the paths thereof be peaceable.
3.18: It is a tree of life to them that take it; and he that holdeth it, is blessed.
3.19: The Lord founded the earth by wisdom; he stablished heavens by prudence.
3.20: The depths of waters brake out by his wisdom; and clouds waxed alto-gether with dew.
3.21: My son, these things float not away [[or not flow away]] from thine eyes; keep thou my law, and my counsel;
3.22: and life shall be to thy soul, and grace to thy cheeks.
3.23: Then thou shalt go trustily in thy way; and thy foot shall not stumble.
3.24: If thou shalt sleep, thou shalt not dread; thou shalt rest, and thy sleep shall be soft [[or and sweet shall be thy sleep]].
3.25: Dread thou not of sudden fear, and the powers of wicked men falling in on thee.
3.26: For the Lord shall be at thy side; and he shall keep thy foot, that thou be not taken.
3.27: Do not thou forbid to do well him that may; if thou mayest, also do thou well.
3.28: Say thou not to thy friend, Go, and turn again, and tomorrow I shall give to thee; when thou mayest give anon.
3.29: Imagine thou not evil to thy friend, when he hath trust in thee.
3.30: Strive thou not against a man without cause, when he doeth none evil to thee.
3.31: Pursue thou not an unjust [[or unrightwise]] man, pursue [[or follow]] thou not his ways.
3.32: For each deceiver is abomination to the Lord; and his speaking is with simple men.
3.33: Neediness is sent of the Lord in the house of a wicked man; but the dwelling places of just [[or rightwise]] men shall be blessed.
3.34: He shall scorn [[the]] scorners; and he shall give grace to mild men.
3.35: Wise men shall have glory; [[the]] enhancing of fools is shame.

4.1: Sons, hear ye the teaching of your father; and perceive ye, that ye know prudence.
4.2: I shall give to you a good gift; forsake ye not my law.
4.3: For why and I was the son of my father, a tender son, and one begotten, before my mother.
4.4: And my father taught me, and said, Thine heart receive my words; keep thou my behests, and thou shalt live.
4.5: Wield thou wisdom, wield thou prudence; forget thou not, neither bow thou away from the words of my mouth.
4.6: Forsake thou not it, and it shall keep thee; love thou it, and it shall keep thee.
4.7: The beginning of wisdom, wield thou wisdom; and in all thy possession, get thou prudence.
4.8: Take thou it, and it shall enhance thee; thou shalt be glorified of it, when thou hast embraced it.
4.9: It shall give increasings of graces to thine head; and a noble crown shall defend thee.
4.10: My son, hear thou, and take my words; that the years of life be multiplied to thee.
4.11: I shall show to thee the way of wisdom; and I shall lead thee by the paths of equity.
4.12: Into which when thou hast entered, thy goings shall not be made strait; and thou shalt run, and shalt not have hurting.
4.13: Hold thou teaching, and forsake [[thou]] it not; keep thou it, for it is thy life.
4.14: Delight thou not in the paths of wicked men; and the way of evil men please not thee.
4.15: Flee thou from it, and pass thou not thereby; bow thou away, and forsake it.
4.16: For they sleep not, no but they have done evil; and sleep is ravished from them, no but they have deceived simple men.
4.17: They eat the bread of unpiety, and drink the wine of wickedness.
4.18: But the path of just [[or rightwise]] men goeth forth as light shining, and increaseth till to [[a]] perfect day.
4.19: The way of wicked men is dark; they know not where they shall fall.
4.20: My son, hearken thou to my words; and bow down thine ears to my speeches.
4.21: Go not they away from thine eyes; keep thou them in the middle of thine heart.
4.22: For those be life to men finding those, and health of all flesh.
4.23: With all keeping keep thine heart, for life cometh forth of it.
4.24: Remove thou a shrewd mouth from thee; and backbiting lips be far from thee.
4.25: Thine eyes see rightful [[or right]] things; and thine eyelids go before thy steps.
4.26: Address thou [[the]] paths to thy feet, and all thy ways shall be stablished.
4.27: Bow thou not to the right side, neither to the left side; turn away thy foot from evil.

5.1: My son, perceive thou my wisdom, and bow down thine ear to my prudence;
5.2: that thou keep thy thoughts, and thy lips keep teaching.
5.3: Give thou not attention to the falseness of a woman; for the lips of an whore be an honeycomb dropping, and her throat is clearer than oil;
5.4: but the last things [[of her]] be bitter as wormwood, and her tongue is sharp as a sword carving, or cutting, on each side.
5.5: Her feet go down into death; and her steps pierce to hells [[or to hell]].
5.6: Those [[or they]] go not by the path of life; her steps be uncertain, and may not be sought out.
5.7: Now therefore, my son, hear thou me, and go thou not away from the words of my mouth.
5.8: Make far thy way from her, and nigh thou not to the doors of her house.
5.9: Give thou not thine honour to aliens, and thy years to the cruel;
5.10: lest peradventure strangers be filled with thy strengths, and lest thy travails be in an alien’s house;
5.11: and thou bewail in the last days, when thou hast wasted thy flesh, and thy body;
5.12: and say, Why loathed I teaching, and mine heart assented not to blamings;
5.13: neither I heard the voice of men teaching me, and I bowed not down mine ear to masters?
5.14: Almost I was in all-evil, in the midst of the church, and of the synagogue.
5.15: Drink thou water of thy cistern, and the floods of thy well.
5.16: Thy wells be streamed forth; and part thy waters in streets.
5.17: Have thou alone them [[or them alone]]; and aliens be not thy partners.
5.18: Thy vein be blessed; and be thou glad with the woman of thy young waxing age.
5.19: An hind most dearworthy; and an hart calf most acceptable. Her teats fill thee in all time; and delight thou continually in the love of her.
5.20: My son, why art thou deceived of an alien woman; and art fostered in the bosom of another?
5.21: The Lord seeth the ways of a man; and he beholdeth all his steps.
5.22: The wickednesses of a wicked man take him; and he is bound with the ropes of his sins.
5.23: He shall die, for he had not learning, and he shall be deceived in the muchliness of his folly.

6.1: My son, if thou hast promised for thy friend, thou hast fastened thine hand at a stranger.
6.2: Thou art bound by the words of thy mouth; and thou art taken with thine own words.
6.3: Therefore, my son, do thou that that I say, and deliver thyself; for thou hast fallen into the hand of thy neighbour. Run thou about, haste thou, raise thy friend;
6.4: give thou not sleep to thine eyes, neither thine eyelids nap.
6.5: Be thou ravished, as a doe from the hand; and as a bird from [[the]] ambushings of the fowler.
6.6: O! thou slow man, go to the ant; and behold thou his ways, and learn thou wisdom.
6.7: Which when he hath no duke, neither commander, nor prince;
6.8: maketh ready in summer meat to himself, and gathereth together in harvest that, that he shall eat.
6.9: How long shalt thou, slow man, sleep? when shalt thou rise from thy sleep?
6.10: A little thou shalt sleep, a little thou shalt nap; a little thou shalt join together thine hands that thou sleep.
6.11: And then neediness, as a way-goer, shall come to thee; and poverty, as an armed man. Forsooth if thou art not slow, thy ripe corn shall come as a well; and neediness shall flee far from thee.
6.12: A man apostate, is a man unprofit-able, he goeth with a wayward mouth;
6.13: he beckoneth with eyes, he trampeth with the foot, he speaketh with the finger,
6.14: by shrewd heart he imagineth evil, and in all time he soweth dissensions.
6.15: His perdition shall come to him anon, and he shall be broken suddenly; and he shall no more have medicine.
6.16: Six things there be, which the Lord hateth; and his soul curseth the seventh thing.
6.17: High eyes, a tongue liar, that is, accustomable to deadly leasing, hands shedding out innocent blood,
6.18: an heart imagining full wicked thoughts, feet swift to run into evil,
6.19: a man bringing forth leasing, a false witness; and him that soweth discord among brethren.
6.20: My son, keep the commandments of thy father; and forsake [[thou]] not the law of thy mother.
6.21: Bind thou those continually in thine heart; and encompass to thy throat.
6.22: When thou goest, go they with thee; when thou sleepest, keep they thee; and thou waking, speak with them.
6.23: For the commandment of God is a lantern, and the law is light, and the blaming of teaching is the way of life;
6.24: that they keep thee from an evil woman, and from a flattering tongue of a strange woman.
6.25: Thine heart covet not the fairness of her; neither be thou taken by the beckonings of her.
6.26: For the price of a whore is scarcely a gobbet of bread; but such a woman taketh the precious soul of a man.
6.27: Whether a man may hide fire in his bosom, that his clothes burn not;
6.28: either go on coals, and his feet be not burnt?
6.29: So he that entereth to the wife of his neighbour; shall not be clean, when he hath touched her.
6.30: It is no great sin, when a man stealeth; for he stealeth to fill an hungry soul.
6.31: And he taken shall yield the seventhfold; and he shall give all the chattel [[or substance]] of his house, and shall deliver himself.
6.32: But he that is an adulterer, shall lose his soul, for the poverty of heart, that is, wanting of reason.
6.33: He gathereth filth, and scandal to himself; and his shame shall not be done away.
6.34: For the fervent love and strong vengeance of the man shall not spare in the day of vengeance,
6.35: neither shall assent to the prayers of any; neither he shall take many gifts for ransom.

7.1: My son, keep thou my words; and keep my behests to thee.
7.2: Keep thou my behests, and thou shalt live; and my law, as the apple of thine eye.
7.3: Bind thou it in thy fingers; write thou it in the tables of thine heart.
7.4: Say thou to wisdom, Thou art my sister; and call thou prudence thy love.
7.5: That it keep thee from a strange woman; and from an alien woman, that maketh her words sweet.
7.6: For she saith, For why from the window of mine house, by the lattice, I beheld;
7.7: and I see little children, that is, fools that have little wit. I behold a young man coward [[or the sorry-hearted young man]],
7.8: that passeth by [[or through]] the streets, beside the corner; and he goeth nigh the way of her house,
7.9: in dark time, when the day draweth to night, in the darkness and mist in the night.
7.10: And lo! a woman, made ready with ornament of an whore to deceive souls, meeteth him,
7.11: and she is a jangler, and going about, and unpatient of rest, and may not stand in the house with her feet;
7.12: and now withoutforth, now in [[the]] streets, now beside [[the]] corners, she ambusheth.
7.13: And she taketh, and kisseth the young man; and flattereth with wooing cheer, that is, unrestfully, and without shame, and saith,
7.14: I owed sacrifices for health; today I have yielded my vows.
7.15: Therefore I went out into thy meeting, and I desired to see thee; and I have found thee.
7.16: I have made my bed with cords, I have arrayed it with tapets painted [[or with painted tapets]] of Egypt;
7.17: I have besprinkled my bed with myrrh, and aloes, and canel.
7.18: Come thou, be we filled with touching of teats, and use we embracings that be coveted; till the day begin to be clear.
7.19: For mine husband is not in his house; he is gone a full long way.
7.20: He took with him a bag of money; he shall turn again into his house in the day of [[the]] full moon.
7.21: She bound him with many words; and she drew forth him with flatterings of lips.
7.22: Anon he as an ox led to slain sacrifice pursueth [[or followeth]] her, and as a jolly lamb and unknowing; and the fool knoweth not, that he is drawn to bonds,
7.23: till an arrow pierce his maw. As if a bird hasteth to the snare; and knoweth not, that it is done of the peril of his life.
7.24: Now therefore, my son, hear thou me; and perceive the words of my mouth.
7.25: Lest thy soul be drawn away in the ways of her; neither be thou deceived in the paths of her.
7.26: For she hath cast down many wounded men; and all [[the]] strongest men were slain of her.
7.27: The ways of hell is her house; and pierce into the inner things of death.

8.1: Whether wisdom crieth not oft; and prudence giveth her voice?
8.2: In most sovereign and high tops, above the way, in the midst of paths,
8.3: and it standeth beside the gates of the city, in those enclosings, and speaketh, and saith,
8.4: A! ye men, I cry oft to you; and my voice is to the sons of men.
8.5: Little children, that is, little of wit, understand ye wisdom; and ye unwise men, perceiveth in heart.
8.6: Hear ye, for I shall speak of great things; and my lips shall be opened, to preach rightful [[or even]] things.
8.7: My throat shall bethink truth; and my lips shall curse a wicked man.
8.8: My words be just; no shrewd thing, neither wayward is in those.
8.9: They be rightful [[or right]] to them that understand; and they be even to them that find knowing.
8.10: Take ye my chastising [[or my discipline]], and not money; choose ye teaching, more than treasure.
8.11: For wisdom is better than all riches most precious; and all desirable thing may not be comparisoned thereto.
8.12: I, wisdom, dwell in counsel; and I am among learned thoughts.
8.13: The dread of the Lord hateth evil; I curse boast, and pride, and a shrewd way, and a double-tongued mouth.
8.14: Counsel is mine, and equity; prudence is mine, and strength.
8.15: Kings reign by me; and makers of laws deem just things by me.
8.16: Princes command by me; and mighty men deem rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] by me.
8.17: I love them that love me; and they that wake early to me, shall find me.
8.18: With me be riches, and glory; sovereign riches, and rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
8.19: My fruit is better than gold, and precious stone; and my seeds [[or my burgeonings]] be better than chosen silver.
8.20: I go in the ways of rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]], in the midst of the paths of doom;
8.21: that I make rich them that love me, and that I fill their treasures or their treasuries.
8.22: The Lord wielded me in the beginning of his ways; before that he made anything, at the beginning.
8.23: From without beginning I was ordained; and from eld [[or old]] times, before that the earth was made.
8.24: [[The]] Depths of waters were not yet; and I was conceived then. The wells of waters had not broken out yet,
8.25: and hills stood not altogether yet by firm heaviness; before little hills I was born.
8.26: Yet he had not made [[the]] earth; and floods, and the earths of the world.
8.27: When he made ready heavens, I was present; when he compassed [[or enclosed]] the depths of waters by certain law and compass.
8.28: When he made steadfast the air above; and weighed the wells of waters.
8.29: When he compassed to the sea his mark; and setted [[or put]] law to waters, that they should not pass their coasts. When he weighed the foundaments of [[the]] earth;
8.30: I was making all things with him. And I delighted by all days, and played before him in all time,
8.31: and I played in the world; and my delights be to be with the sons of men.
8.32: Now, therefore, sons, hear ye me; blessed be they that keep my ways.
8.33: Hear ye teaching, and be ye wise men; and do not ye cast it away.
8.34: Blessed is the man that heareth me, and that watcheth at my gates all day; and keepeth [[or waiteth]] at the posts of my door[[s]].
8.35: He that findeth me, shall find life; and he shall draw health of the Lord.
8.36: But he that sinneth against me shall hurt his soul; all that hate me, love death.

9.1: Wisdom builded an house to himself; he hewed out seven pillars,
9.2: he offered his slain sacrifices, he meddled [[or mingled]] wine, and setted [[or set]] forth his table.
9.3: He sent his handmaids, that they should call to the tower; and to the walls of the city.
9.4: If any man is little in wit, come he to me. And wisdom spake to unwise men,
9.5: Come ye, eat ye my bread; and drink ye the wine, which I have meddled [[or mingled]] to you.
9.6: Forsake ye young childhood, and live ye; and go ye by the way of prudence.
9.7: He that teacheth a scorner, doeth wrong to himself; and he that reproveth a wicked man, engendereth a wem to himself.
9.8: Do not thou reprove a scorner; lest he hate thee. Reprove thou a wise man; and he shall love thee.
9.9: Give thou occasion to a wise man; and wisdom shall be increased to him. Teach thou a just [[or rightwise]] man; and he shall hasten to take it.
9.10: The beginning of wisdom is the dread of the Lord; and prudence is the knowing of saints.
9.11: For thy days shall be multiplied by me; and [[the]] years of life shall be increased to thee.
9.12: If thou art wise, thou shalt be wise to thyself, and to thy neighbours. Forsooth if thou art a scorner, thou alone shalt bear evil.
9.13: A fond [[or foolish]] woman, and full of cry, and full of unleaveful lusts, and that knoweth nothing utterly,
9.14: sitteth in the doors of her house, on a seat, in an high place of the city;
9.15: to call men passing by the way, and men going in their journey.
9.16: Who is a little man in wit; bow he to me. And she spake to a coward [[or to the sorry-hearted]],
9.17: Waters of theft be sweeter, and bread hid is sweeter. [[Stolen waters be sweeter, and hid bread more sweet.]]
9.18: And [[he]] knew not that giants be there; and the guests of her be in the depths of hell. Soothly he that shall be applied, either fastened, to her, shall go down to hells [[or shall fall down into hell]]. For why he that goeth away from her shall be saved.

10.1: The parables of Solomon. A wise son maketh glad his father; but a fond [[or foolish]] son is the sorrow of his mother.
10.2: Treasures of wickedness shall not profit; but rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] shall deliver from death.
10.3: The Lord shall not torment the soul of a just [[or rightwise]] man with hunger; and he shall destroy the treasons of unpious men.
10.4: A slow hand hath wrought needi-ness; but the hand of strong men maketh ready riches. Forsooth he that enforceth or endeavoureth to get any-thing by leasings, feedeth the winds; soothly the same man pursueth birds flying [[or followeth flying birds]].
10.5: He that gathereth together in harvest, is a wise son; but he that sleepeth in summer, is a son of confusion.
10.6: The blessing of God is over the head of a just [[or rightwise]] man; but wickedness covereth the mouth of wicked men.
10.7: The mind or memory of a just [[or rightwise]] man shall be with praisings; and the name of wicked men shall wax rotten.
10.8: A wise man shall receive commandments with heart; a fool is beaten with his own lips.
10.9: He that goeth simply, goeth trustily; but he that maketh shrewd his ways, shall be [[made]] open.
10.10: He that beckoneth with the eye, shall give sorrow; a fool shall be beaten with his own lips.
10.11: The vein of life is the mouth of a just [[or rightwise]] man; but the mouth of wicked men covereth wickedness.
10.12: Hatred raiseth up chidings; and charity covereth all sins.
10.13: Wisdom is found in the lips of a wise man; and a rod in the back of him that is needy of heart.
10.14: Wise men hide knowing; but the mouth of a fool is next to confusion.
10.15: The chattel [[or substance]] of a rich man is the city of his strength; the dread of poor men is the neediness of them.
10.16: The work of a just [[or rightwise]] man is to life; but the fruit of a wicked man is to sin.
10.17: The way of life is to him that keepeth chastising [[or discipline]]; but he that forsaketh blamings, erreth.
10.18: False lips hide hatred; he that bringeth forth despising is unwise.
10.19: Sin shall not fail in much speaking; but he that measureth his lips, is most prudent.
10.20: Chosen silver is the tongue of a just [[or rightwise]] man; the heart of wicked men is for nought.
10.21: The lips of a just [[or rightwise]] man teach full many men; but they that be unlearned shall die in neediness of heart.
10.22: The blessing of the Lord maketh rich men; and torment shall not be fellowshipped to them.
10.23: A fool worketh wickedness as by laughing; but wisdom is prudence to a man or but prudence is to a wise man.
10.24: That that a wicked man dreadeth, shall come [[up]] on him; the desire of just [[or rightwise]] men shall be given to them.
10.25: As a tempest passing, a wicked man shall not be; but a just [[or rightwise]] man shall be as an ever-lasting foundament.
10.26: As vinegar annoyeth the teeth, and smoke the eyes; so a slow man annoyeth them that sent him in the way.
10.27: The dread of the Lord increaseth days; and the years of wicked men shall be made short.
10.28: Abiding of just [[or rightwise]] men is gladness; but the hope of wicked men shall perish.
10.29: The strength of a simple man is the way of the Lord; and dread to them that work evil.
10.30: A just [[or rightwise]] man shall not be moved without end; but wicked men shall not dwell on the earth.
10.31: The mouth of a just [[or rightwise]] man shall bring forth wisdom; the tongue of shrews shall perish.
10.32: The lips of a just [[or rightwise]] man behold pleasant things; and the mouth of wicked men beholdeth wayward [[or perverted]] things.

11.1: A guileful balance is abomination with God; and an even weight is his will.
11.2: Where pride is, there also despising shall be; but where meekness is, there also is wisdom.
11.3: The simpleness of just [[or rightwise]] men shall dress them; and the deceiving of wayward men shall destroy them.
11.4: Riches shall not profit in the day of vengeance; but rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] shall deliver from death.
11.5: The rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]] of a simple man shall dress his way; and a wicked man shall fall in his wickedness.
11.6: The rightfulness of rightful men [[or The rightwiseness of right men]] shall deliver them; and wicked men shall be taken in their ambushings.
11.7: When a wicked man is dead, none hope shall be further of him; and [[the]] abiding of busy men in evil shall perish.
11.8: A just [[or rightwise]] man is delivered from anguish; and a wicked man shall be given for him.
11.9: A feigner by mouth deceiveth his friend; but just [[or rightwise]] men shall be delivered by [[or with]] knowing.
11.10: A city shall be enhanced in the goods of just [[or rightwise]] men; and praising shall be in the perdition of wicked men.
11.11: A city shall be enhanced by [[the]] blessing of just [[or rightwise]] men; and it shall be destroyed by the mouth of wicked men.
11.12: He that despiseth his friend, is needy in heart; but a prudent man shall be still.
11.13: He that goeth guilefully, showeth privates; but he that is faithful, covereth the private matter of a friend.
11.14: Where a governor is not, the people shall fall; but health is, where be many counsels.
11.15: He that maketh faith, that is, obligation, for a stranger, shall be tormented with evil; but he that escheweth snares, shall be secure.
11.16: A gracious woman shall find glory; and strong men shall have riches.
11.17: A merciful man doeth well to his soul; but he that is cruel, casteth away, yea, kinsmen.
11.18: A wicked man maketh unstable work; but faithful meed is to him, that soweth rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
11.19: Mercy shall make ready life; and the pursuing [[or the following]] of evil, death.
11.20: A shrewd heart is abominable to the Lord; and his will is in them, that go simply.
11.21: Though hand be in hand, an evil man shall not be innocent; but the seed of just [[or rightwise]] men shall be saved.
11.22: A golden ring in the nostrils of a sow, is a woman fair and [[a]] fool.
11.23: The desire of just [[or rightwise]] men is all good; abiding of wicked men is strong vengeance.
11.24: Some men part their own things, and be made richer; other men ravish things, that be not theirs, and they be ever in neediness.
11.25: A soul that blesseth, shall be made fat; and he that filleth, shall be filled also.
11.26: He that hideth wheat, shall be cursed among the peoples; but blessing shall come [[up]] on the heads of sellers.
11.27: Well be he who riseth early, that seeketh good things; but he that is a searcher of evils, shall be oppressed of those [[or of them]].
11.28: He that trusteth in his riches, shall fall; but just [[or rightwise]] men shall burgeon as a green leaf.
11.29: He that troubleth his house, shall have winds in possession; and he that is a fool, shall serve a wise man.
11.30: The fruit of a rightful [[or rightwise]] man is the tree of life; and he that taketh souls, is a wise man.
11.31: If a just [[or rightwise]] man receiveth in [[the]] earth, how much more an unfaithful man, and a sinner.

12.1: He that loveth chastising [[or discipline]], loveth knowing; but he that hateth blamings, is unwise.
12.2: He that is good, shall draw to himself grace of the Lord; but he that trusteth in his thoughts, doeth wickedly.
12.3: A man shall not be made strong by wickedness; and the root of just [[or rightwise]] men shall not be moved.
12.4: A diligent woman is a crown to her husband; and rot is in the bones of that woman, that doeth things worthy of confusion.
12.5: The thoughts of just [[or rightwise]] men be dooms; and the counsels of wicked men be guileful.
12.6: The words of wicked men set treason to blood; the mouth of just [[or rightwise]] men shall deliver them.
12.7: Overturn thou wicked men, and they shall not be; but the houses of just [[or rightwise]] men shall dwell perfectly.
12.8: A man shall be known by his teaching; but he that is vain and heartless, shall be open to despising.
12.9: Better is a poor man, and sufficient to himself, than a glorious man, and needy of bread.
12.10: A just [[or rightwise]] man knoweth the lives of his work beasts; but the entrails of wicked men be cruel.
12.11: He that worketh his land, shall be filled with loaves; but he that pursueth [[or followeth]] idleness, is most foolish. He that is sweet, that is mild, liveth in temperances; and in his admonishings he forsaketh despisings.
12.12: The desire of a wicked man is the memorial of worst things; but the root of just [[or rightwise]] men shall increase.
12.13: For the sins of lips, falling down nigheth to an evil man; but a just [[or rightwise]] man shall escape from anguish.
12.14: Of the fruit of his mouth each man shall be [[ful]] filled with goods; and by the works of his hands it shall be yielded to him.
12.15: The way of a fool is rightful [[or right]] in his eyes; but he that is wise, heareth counsels.
12.16: A fool showeth anon his ire; but he that dissembleth wrongs, is wise.
12.17: He that speaketh that, that he knoweth, is a judge of rightfulness [[or of rightwiseness]]; but he that lieth, is a guileful witness.
12.18: A man is that promiseth, and he is pricked as with the sword of conscience; but the tongue of wise men is health.
12.19: The lip of truth shall be steadfast without end; but he that is a sudden witness, maketh ready the tongue of leasing.
12.20: Guile is in the heart of them that think evils; but joy pursueth [[or followeth]] them that make counsels of peace.
12.21: Whatever befalleth to a just [[or rightwise]] man, it shall not make him sorry [[or sorrow]]; but wicked men shall be filled with evil.
12.22: False lips is abomination to the Lord; but they that do faithfully, please him.
12.23: A fell man covereth knowing; and the heart of unwise men stirreth folly.
12.24: The hand of strong men shall have lordship; but the hand that is slow, shall serve to tributes.
12.25: Mourning in the heart of a just [[or rightwise]] man shall make him meek; and he shall be made glad by a good word.
12.26: He that despiseth harm for a friend, is a just [[or rightwise]] man; but the way of wicked men shall deceive them.
12.27: A guileful man shall not find winning; and the substance of a diligent man shall be the price of gold, that is, preciouser than gold.
12.28: Life is in the path of rightwiseness; but the wrong way leadeth to death.

13.1: A wise son is the teaching of the father; but he that is a scorner, heareth not, when he is reproved.
13.2: A man shall be filled with goods of the fruit of his mouth; but the soul of unpious men is wicked.
13.3: He that keepeth his mouth, keepeth his soul; but he that is unwary to speak, shall feel evils.
13.4: A slow man will, and will not; but the soul of them that work shall be made fat.
13.5: A just [[or rightwise]] man shall loathe a false word; but a wicked man shameth, and shall be shamed.
13.6: Rightfulness [[or Rightwiseness]] keepeth the way of an innocent man; but wickedness deceiveth a sinner.
13.7: A man is as rich, when he hath nothing; and a man is as poor, when he is in many riches.
13.8: [[The]] Redemption of the soul of [[a]] man is his riches; but he that is poor, suffereth not blaming.
13.9: The light of just [[or rightwise]] men maketh glad; but the lantern of wicked men shall be quenched.
13.10: Strives be ever among proud men; but they that do all things with counsel, be governed by wisdom.
13.11: Hasted chattel [[or substance]], that is, gotten hastily, shall be made less; but that that is gathered little and little with hand, shall be multiplied.
13.12: Hope which is delayed, tormenteth the soul; a tree of life is desire coming.
13.13: He that backbiteth anything, bindeth himself into [[the]] time to coming [[or to come]]; but he that dreadeth the commandment, shall live in peace.
13.14: The law of a wise man is a well of life; that he bow away from the falling of death, that is, of sin, and of hell.
13.15: Good teaching shall give grace; a swallow is in the way of despisers.
13.16: A fell [[or witting]] man doeth all things with counsel; but he that is a fool, shall open folly.
13.17: The messenger of a wicked man shall fall into evil; a faithful messenger is health.
13.18: Neediness and shame is to him that forsaketh teaching; but he that assenteth to a blamer, shall be glorified.
13.19: Desire, if it is [[ful]] filled, delighteth the soul; fools loathe them that flee evils.
13.20: He that goeth with wise men, shall be wise; the friend of fools shall be made like them.
13.21: Evil pursueth sinners; and goods shall be given to just [[or rightwise]] men.
13.22: A good man shall leave after him heirs, sons, and the sons of sons; and the chattel [[or substance]] of a sinner is kept to a just [[or rightwise]] man.
13.23: Many meats be in the newly-tilled fields of fathers; and be gathered to other men without doom.
13.24: He that spareth the rod, hateth his son; but he that loveth him, teacheth busily.
13.25: A just [[or rightwise]] man eateth, and [[ful]] filleth his soul; but the womb of wicked men is unable to be filled.

14.1: A wise woman buildeth her house; and an unwise woman shall destroy with hands, that is, with her evil works, an house builded.
14.2: A man going in rightful [[or right]] way, and dreading God, is despised of him that goeth in the way of evil fame.
14.3: The rod of pride is in the mouth of a fool; the lips of wise men keep them.
14.4: Where oxen be not, the cratch is void; but where full many corns appear, there the strength of the ox is [[made]] open.
14.5: A faithful witness shall not lie; a guileful witness bringeth forth a leasing.
14.6: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and he findeth it not; the teaching of prudent men is easy.
14.7: Go thou against a man a fool; and he shall not know the lips of prudence.
14.8: The wisdom of a fell [[or witting]] man is to understand his way; and the unwariness of fools erreth.
14.9: A fool scorneth sin; grace shall dwell among just [[or rightwise]] men.
14.10: The heart that knoweth the bitter-ness of his soul; a stranger shall not be meddled [[or mingled]] in the joy thereof.
14.11: The house of wicked men shall be done away; the tabernacles of just [[or rightwise]] men shall burgeon.
14.12: Soothly a way is, that seemeth just [[or rightwise]] to a man; but the last things thereof lead forth to death.
14.13: Laughing shall be meddled [[or mingled]] with sorrow; and mourning occupieth the last things of joy.
14.14: A fool shall be filled with his ways; and a good man shall be above him.
14.15: An innocent man believeth to each word; a fell [[or witting]] man beholdeth his goings.
14.16: A wise man dreadeth, and boweth away from evil; a fool skippeth over, and trusteth.
14.17: A man unpatient shall work folly; and a guileful man is odious.
14.18: Little men of wit shall hold folly; and fell [[or witting]] men shall abide knowing.
14.19: Evil men shall lie down before good men; and unpious men before the gates of just [[or rightwise]] men.
14.20: A poor man shall be hateful, yea, to his neighbour; but many men be friends of rich men.
14.21: He that despiseth his neighbour, doeth sin; but he that doeth mercy to a poor man, shall be blessed.
14.22: He that believeth in the Lord, loveth mercy; they err that work evil. Mercy and truth make ready goods;
14.23: abundance shall be in each good work or in every good work. Soothly where full many words be, there neediness is oft.
14.24: The crown of wise men is the riches of them; the folly of fools is unwariness.
14.25: A faithful witness delivereth souls; and a false man bringeth forth leasings.
14.26: In the dread of the Lord is trust of strength; and hope shall be to the sons of him.
14.27: The dread of the Lord is a well of life; that it bow away from the falling of death.
14.28: The dignity of the king is in the multitude of people; and the shame of a prince is in the fewness of people.
14.29: He that is patient, is governed by much wisdom; but he that is unpatient, enhanceth his folly.
14.30: Health of heart is the life of flesh; envy is [[the]] rot of bones.
14.31: He that falsely challengeth a needy man, despiseth his Maker; but he that hath mercy on a poor man, honoureth his Maker.
14.32: A wicked man is put out for his malice; but a just [[or rightwise]] man hopeth in his death.
14.33: Wisdom resteth in the heart of a wise man; and he shall teach all unlearned men.
14.34: Rightfulness [[or Rightwiseness]] raiseth [[up]] a folk; sin maketh peoples wretches.
14.35: A servant understanding is accept-able to a king; a servant unprofitable shall suffer the wrathfulness of him.

15.1: A soft answer breaketh ire; an hard word raiseth strong vengeance.
15.2: The tongue of wise men honoureth knowing; the mouth of fools boileth out folly.
15.3: In each place the eyes of the Lord behold good men, and evil men.
15.4: A pleasant tongue is the tree of life; but the tongue that is unmeasurable [[or untempered]], shall defoul the spirit.
15.5: A fool scorneth the teaching of his father; but he that keepeth blamings, shall be made wiser. Most virtue shall be in plenteous rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]]; but the thoughts of wicked men shall be drawn up by the root.
15.6: The house of a just [[or rightwise]] man is full great strength; and troubling is in the fruits of a wicked man.
15.7: The lips of wise men shall sow abroad knowing; the hearts of fools shall be unlike, that is, they shall be full of ignorance.
15.8: The sacrifices of wicked men be abominable to the Lord; the avows of just men [[or the vows of rightwise men]] be pleasant.
15.9: The life of the unpious man is abomination to the Lord; he that pur-sueth rightfulness [[or followeth right-wiseness]], shall be loved of the Lord.
15.10: Evil teaching is of men that forsake the way of life; he that hateth blamings shall die.
15.11: Hell and perdition be open before the Lord; how much more the hearts of [[the]] sons of men.
15.12: A man full of pestilence loveth not him that reproveth him; and he goeth not to wise men.
15.13: A joyful heart maketh glad the face; the spirit is cast down in the mourning of soul.
15.14: The heart of a wise man seeketh teaching; and the mouth of fools is fed with unknowing.
15.15: All the days of a poor man be evil; a secure soul is a continual feast.
15.16: Better is a little with the dread of the Lord, than many treasures and unfillable.
15.17: It is better to be called to worts with charity, than with hatred to a calf made fat.
15.18: A wrathful man raiseth chidings; he that is patient, assuageth chidings that were raised.
15.19: The way of slow men is as an hedge of thorns; the way of just [[or rightwise]] men is without [[thing of]] hurting.
15.20: A wise son maketh glad his father; but a fond [[or foolish]] man despiseth his mother.
15.21: Folly is joy to a fool; but a prudent man shall address his steps.
15.22: Thoughts be destroyed, where no counsel is; but where many counsellors be, they be confirmed.
15.23: A man is glad in the sentence of his mouth; and a covenable word is best.
15.24: The path of life is on a learned man; that he bow away from the last hell.
15.25: The Lord shall destroy the house of proud men; and he shall make steadfast the coasts of a widow.
15.26: Evil thoughts is abomination of the Lord; and a clean word most fair shall be made steadfast of him.
15.27: He that pursueth [[or followeth]] avarice, troubleth his house; but he that hateth gifts shall live. Sins be purged by mercy and faith; each man boweth away from evil by the dread of the Lord.
15.28: The soul of a just [[or rightwise]] man bethinketh obedience; the mouth of wicked men is full of evils.
15.29: The Lord is far from wicked men; and he shall hear the prayers of just [[or rightwise]] men.
15.30: The light of eyes maketh glad the soul; good fame maketh fat the bones.
15.31: The ear that heareth the blamings of life, shall dwell in the midst of wise men.
15.32: He that casteth away chastising [[or discipline]], despiseth his soul; but he that assenteth to blamings, is a peaceable holder of the heart.
15.33: The dread of the Lord is teaching of wisdom; and meekness goeth before glory.

16.1: It pertaineth to man to make ready the soul; and it pertaineth to the Lord to govern the tongue.
16.2: All the ways of men be open to the eyes of God; the Lord is a weigher of spirits, that is, of wills, yielding to man after his deservings.
16.3: Show thy works to the Lord; and thy thoughts shall be addressed.
16.4: The Lord wrought all things for himself; and he made ready a wicked man to the evil day.
16.5: Abomination of the Lord is each proud man; yea, though the hand is to the hand, he shall not be innocent. The beginning of [[the]] good way is to do rightwiseness; forsooth it is more acceptable with God, than to offer sacrifices.
16.6: Wickedness is again-bought by mercy and truth; and men boweth away from evil by the dread of the Lord.
16.7: When the ways of a man please the Lord, he shall convert, yea, his enemies to peace.
16.8: Better is a little with rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]], than many fruits with wickedness.
16.9: The heart of a man shall dispose his way; but it pertaineth to the Lord to dress his steps.
16.10: Divining is in the lips of a king; his mouth shall not err in doom.
16.11: The dooms of the Lord be weight and balance; and his works be all the stones of the world.
16.12: They that do wickedly be abominable to the king; for the throne of the realm is made steadfast by rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
16.13: The will of kings is just [[or rightwise]] lips; he that speaketh rightful [[or right]] things, shall be addressed.
16.14: [[The]] Indignation of the king is messengers of death; and a wise man shall please him.
16.15: Life is in gladness of the king’s cheer; and his mercy is as rain coming late.
16.16: Wield thou wisdom, for it is better than gold; and get thou prudence, for it is preciouser than silver.
16.17: The path of just [[or rightwise]] men boweth away from evils; the keeper of his soul keepeth his way.
16.18: Pride goeth before sorrow; and the spirit shall be enhanced before falling.
16.19: It is better to be made meek with mild men, than to part spoils with proud men.
16.20: A learned man in word shall find goods; and he that hopeth in the Lord is blessed.
16.21: He that is wise in heart, shall be called prudent; and he that is sweet in speech, shall find greater things.
16.22: The well of life is the learning of him that wieldeth; the teaching of fools is folly.
16.23: The heart of a wise man shall teach his mouth; and shall increase grace to his lips.
16.24: Words well-set together is a comb of honey; health of bones is the sweetness of soul.
16.25: A way there is that seemeth rightful [[or right]] to a man; and the last things thereof lead to death.
16.26: The soul of a man travailing travaileth to himself; for his mouth compelled him.
16.27: An unwise man diggeth for evil; and fire burneth in his lips.
16.28: A wayward man raiseth strives; and a man full of words separateth princes.
16.29: A wicked man flattereth his friend; and leadeth him by a way not good.
16.30: He that thinketh shrewd things with eyes astonied, biteth his lips, and performeth evil.
16.31: A crown of dignity is eld age, that shall be found in the ways of rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
16.32: A patient man is better than a strong man; and he that is lord of his soul, is better than an overcomer of cities.
16.33: Lots be sent into the bosom; but they be tempered of the Lord.

17.1: Better is a dry morsel with joy, than an house full of sacrifices with chiding.
17.2: A wise servant shall be lord of fond [[or foolish]] sons; and he shall part heritage among brethren.
17.3: As silver is proved by fire, and gold is proved by a chimney, so the Lord proveth hearts.
17.4: An evil man obeyeth to a wicked tongue; and a false man obeyeth to false lips.
17.5: He that despiseth a poor man, reproveth his maker; and he that is glad in the falling of another man, shall not be unpunished.
17.6: The crown of eld [[or old]] men is the sons of sons; and the glory of sons is the fathers of them.
17.7: Words well-set together beseem not a fool; and a lying lip becometh not a prince.
17.8: A precious stone most acceptable is the abiding of him that seeketh; whither ever he turneth himself, he understandeth prudently.
17.9: He that covereth trespass, seeketh friendships; he that rehearseth by an high word, separateth them that be knit together in peace.
17.10: A blaming profiteth more at a prudent man, than an hundred wounds at a fool.
17.11: Ever an evil man seeketh strives; forsooth a cruel angel shall be sent against him.
17.12: It speedeth more to meet a female bear, when her whelps be ravished, than a fool trusting to himself in his folly.
17.13: Evil shall not go away from the house of him, that yieldeth evils for goods.
17.14: He that letteth out water, is the head of strives; and before that he suffereth wrong, he forsaketh doom.
17.15: Both he that justifieth a wicked man, and he that condemneth a just [[or rightwise]] man, ever either is abominable to God.
17.16: What profiteth it to a fool to have riches, since he may not buy wisdom? He that maketh his house high, seeketh falling; and he that escheweth to learn, shall fall into evils.
17.17: He that is a friend, loveth in all time; and a brother is proved in anguishes.
17.18: A fond [[or foolish]] man shall make joy with hands, when he hath promised for his friend.
17.19: He that bethinketh discords, loveth chidings; and he that enhanceth his mouth, seeketh falling.
17.20: He that is of wayward heart, shall not find good; and he that turneth the tongue, shall fall into evil.
17.21: A fool is born in his shame; but neither the father shall be glad in a fool.
17.22: A joyful soul maketh liking age; a sorrowful spirit maketh dry bones.
17.23: A wicked man taketh gifts from the bosom, to mis-turn the paths of doom.
17.24: Wisdom shineth in the face of a prudent man; the eyes of fools be in the ends of earth.
17.25: A fond [[or foolish]] son is the ire [[or the wrath]] of the father, and the sorrow of the mother that bare him.
17.26: It is not good to bring in harm to a just [[or rightwise]] man; neither to smite the prince that deemeth rightfully.
17.27: He that measureth his words, is wise and prudent; and a learned man is of precious spirit.
17.28: Also a fool, if he is still, shall be guessed a wise man; and, if he presseth together his lips, he is guessed an understanding man.

18.1: He that will go away from a friend, seeketh occasions, that is, feigneth causes; in all time he shall be despisable.
18.2: A fool receiveth not the words of prudence; no but thou say those things, that be turned in his heart.
18.3: A wicked man, when he cometh into depth of sins, despiseth whole-some lore, and commandment; but scandal and shame pursueth [[or followeth]] him.
18.4: Deep water is the words of the mouth of a man; and a strand floating over is the well of wisdom.
18.5: It is not good to take the person of a wicked man in doom, that thou bow away from the truth of doom.
18.6: The lips of a fool meddle [[or mingle]] themselves with chidings; and his mouth stirreth strives.
18.7: The mouth of a fool is [[the]] defouling of him; and his lips be the falling of his soul.
18.8: The words of a double-tongued man be as simple; and they come unto the inner things of the womb. Dread casteth down a slow man; forsooth the souls of men turned into women’s condition shall have hunger.
18.9: He that is nesh, and dissolute, either unsteadfast, in his work, is the brother of a man destroying his works.
18.10: A full strong tower is the name of the Lord; a just [[or rightwise]] man runneth to him, and [[he]] shall be enhanced.
18.11: The chattel [[or substance]] of a rich man is the city of his strength; and as a strong wall compassing him.
18.12: The heart of man is enhanced, before that it be broken; and it is made meek, before that it be glorified.
18.13: He that answereth before that he heareth, showeth himself to be a fool; and worthy of shame.
18.14: The spirit of a man sustaineth his feebleness; but who may sustain a spirit light to be wroth?
18.15: The heart of a prudent man shall hold steadfastly knowing; and the ear of wise men seeketh teaching.
18.16: The gift of a man alargeth his way; and maketh space to him before princes.
18.17: A just [[or rightwise]] man is the first accuser of himself; his friend cometh, and shall search him.
18.18: Lot ceaseth against-sayings; and deemeth also among mighty men.
18.19: A brother that is helped of a brother, is as a steadfast city; and [[the]] dooms be as the bars of cities.
18.20: A man’s womb shall be [[ful]] filled of the fruit of his mouth; and the seeds of his lips shall fill him.
18.21: Death and life be in the works of [[the]] tongue; they that love it, shall eat the fruits thereof.
18.22: He that findeth a good woman, findeth a good thing; and of the Lord he shall draw up mirth. He that putteth away a good woman, putteth away a good thing; but he that holdeth an adulteress, is a fool and unwise.
18.23: A poor man shall speak with beseechings; and a rich man shall speak sternly.
18.24: A man friendly to fellowship shall more be a friend, than a brother.

19.1: Better is a poor man, that goeth in his simpleness, than a rich man biting his lips, and unwise.
19.2: Where is not knowing of the soul, there is not good; and he that is hasty, in feet hurteth [[or stumbleth]].
19.3: The folly of a man deceiveth his steps; and he burneth in his soul against God.
19.4: Riches increase full many friends; forsooth also they be departed from a poor man, which he had.
19.5: A false witness shall not be unpunished; and he that speaketh leasings, shall not escape.
19.6: Many men honour the person of a mighty man; and they be friends of him that dealeth gifts.
19.7: The brethren of a poor man hate him; furthermore and the friends went away far from him. He that pursueth [[or followeth]] words only, shall have nothing;
19.8: but he that holdeth stably the mind, loveth his soul, and the keeper of prudence shall find goods.
19.9: A false witness shall not be unpunished; and he that speaketh leasings, shall perish.
19.10: Delights become not a fool; neither it becometh a servant to be lord of princes.
19.11: The teaching of a man is known by patience; and his glory is to pass over wicked things.
19.12: As the gnashing of a lion, so and the ire of the king; and as dew on herb, so and the gladness of the king.
19.13: The sorrow of the father is a fond [[or foolish]] son; and roofs dropping continually is a woman full of chiding.
19.14: Houses and riches be given of father and mother; but a prudent wife is given properly of the Lord.
19.15: Sloth bringeth in sleep; and a negligent soul shall have hunger.
19.16: He that keepeth the commandment of God, keepeth his soul; but he that chargeth not [[or despiseth]] his way, shall be slain.
19.17: He that hath mercy on a poor man, lendeth to the Lord; and he shall yield his while to him.
19.18: Teach thy son, and despair thou not; but set [[or put]] thou not thy soul to the slaying of him.
19.19: Forsooth he that is unpatient, shall suffer harm; and when he hath ravished, he shall lay to another thing.
19.20: Hear thou counsel, and take thou doctrine; that thou be wise in thy last things.
19.21: Many thoughts there be in the heart of a man; but the will of the Lord shall dwell.
19.22: A needy man is merciful; and better is a poor just [[or rightwise]] man, than a man liar.
19.23: Dread of the Lord leadeth to life; and he that dreadeth God shall dwell in plenty, without visiting of the worst or without full evil visiting.
19.24: A slow man hideth his hand under his armpit, and putteth it not to his mouth.
19.25: When a man full of pestilence is beaten, a fool shall be the wiser. If thou blamest a wise man, he shall understand teaching.
19.26: He that tormenteth his father, and fleeth from his mother, shall be full of evil fame, and shall be cursed.
19.27: Son, cease thou not to hear teaching; and know thou the words of knowing.
19.28: A wicked witness scorneth doom; and the mouth of unpious men devoureth wickedness.
19.29: Dooms be made ready to scorners; and hammers smiting be made ready to the bodies of fools.

20.1: Wine is a lecherous thing, and drunkenness is full of noise; whoever delighteth in these, shall not be wise.
20.2: As the roaring of a lion, so and the dread of a king; he that stirreth him to ire, sinneth against his soul.
20.3: It is honour to a man that separateth himself from strivings; but fond men be meddled [[or fools shall be mingled]] with despisings.
20.4: A slow man would not ear for cold; therefore he shall beg in summer, and men shall not give to him.
20.5: As deep water, so counsel is in the heart of a man; but a wise man shall draw it out.
20.6: Many men be called merciful; but who shall find a faithful man?
20.7: Forsooth a just [[or rightwise]] man that goeth in his simpleness, shall leave blessed sons after him.
20.8: A king that sitteth in the seat of doom, destroyeth all evil by his looking.
20.9: Who may say, Mine heart is clean; I am clean of sin?
20.10: A weight, greater in buying, and a weight, lesser in selling, a measure and a measure, ever either is abominable at God.
20.11: A child is understood by his studies, if his works be rightful [[or right]] and clean.
20.12: An ear hearing, and an eye seeing, [[or The hearing ear, and the seeing eye]], God made ever either.
20.13: Do not thou love sleep, lest needi-ness oppress thee; open thine eyes, and be thou [[ful]] filled with loaves.
20.14: Each buyer saith, It is evil, it is evil; and when he hath gone away, then he shall have glory.
20.15: Gold, and the multitude of gems, and a precious vessel, be the lips of knowing.
20.16: Take thou away the cloth of him that was a borrow of another man; and for strangers take thou away a wed from him.
20.17: The bread of a leasing, that is, gotten by a leasing, is sweet to a man; and afterward his mouth shall be filled with reckoning [[or with little pebble stones]].
20.18: Thoughts be made strong by counsels; and battles shall be treated by governances.
20.19: Be thou not meddled [[or mingled]] with him that showeth privates, and goeth guilefully, and alargeth his lips.
20.20: The light of him that curseth his father and mother, shall be quenched in the midst of darknesses.
20.21: Heritage to which men hasteth in the beginning, shall want blessing in the last time.
20.22: Say thou not, I shall yield evil for evil; abide thou the Lord, and he shall deliver thee.
20.23: Abomination with God is weight and weight; a guileful balance is not good.
20.24: The steps of man be dressed of the Lord; who forsooth of men may understand his way?
20.25: Falling of man is to make avow [[or vow]] to saints, and afterward to withdraw the vows.
20.26: A wise king scattereth wicked men; and boweth a bow of victory, that is, a stone bow, over them.
20.27: The lantern of the Lord is the spirit of man, that seeketh out all the privates of the womb.
20.28: Mercy and truth keep a king; and his throne is made strong by meekness.
20.29: The full out joying of young men is the strength of them; and the dignity of eld [[or old]] men is hoariness.
20.30: The wanness of wound shall wipe away evils, and wounds in the privier things of the womb.

21.1: As partings of waters, so the heart of the king is in the power of the Lord; whither ever he will, he shall bow it.
21.2: Each way of a man seemeth rightful [[or right]] to himself; but the Lord weigheth the hearts.
21.3: To do mercy and doom, pleaseth more the Lord, than sacrifices.
21.4: Enhancing of eyes is [[the]] alarging of the heart; the lantern of wicked men is sin.
21.5: The thoughts of a strong man be ever in abundance; but each slow man is ever in neediness.
21.6: He that gathereth treasures by the tongue of a lie maker, is vain, and without heart; and he shall be hurled to the snares of death.
21.7: The ravens of unpious men shall draw them down; for they would not do doom.
21.8: The wayward way of a man is alien from God; but the work of him that is clean of sin, is rightful [[or right]].
21.9: It is better to sit in the corner of an house without roof, than with a woman full of chiding, and in a common house.
21.10: The soul of an unpious man desireth evil; he shall not have mercy on his neighbour.
21.11: When a man full of pestilence is punished, a little man of wit shall be wiser; and if he pursueth [[or follow]] a wise man, he shall take knowing.
21.12: A just [[or rightwise]] man of the house of a wicked man thinketh, to withdraw wicked men from evil.
21.13: He that stoppeth his ear at the cry of a poor man, shall cry also, and he shall not be heard.
21.14: A gift hid quencheth chidings; and a gift in [[the]] bosom quencheth most indignation.
21.15: It is joy to a just [[or rightwise]] man to make doom; and it is dread to them that work wickedness.
21.16: A man that erreth from the way of doctrine, shall dwell in the company of giants, that is, of men evil ruled, either of fiends.
21.17: He that loveth meats, shall be in neediness; he that loveth wine and fat things, shall not be made rich.
21.18: An unpious man shall be given for a just [[or rightwise]] man; and a wicked man shall be given for a rightful [[or the right]] man.
21.19: It is better to dwell in a desert land, than with a woman full of chiding, and wrathful.
21.20: Desirable treasure and oil is in the dwelling place of a just [[or rightwise]] man; and an unprudent man shall destroy it.
21.21: He that pursueth rightfulness [[or followeth rightwiseness]] and mercy, shall find life [[and rightwiseness]] and glory.
21.22: A wise man ascended into the city of strong men, and destroyed the strength of [[the]] trust thereof.
21.23: He that keepeth his mouth and his tongue, keepeth his soul from anguishes.
21.24: A proud man and boaster is called a fool, that worketh pride in ire.
21.25: Desires slay a slow man; for his hands would not work anything.
21.26: All day he coveteth and desireth; but he that is a just [[or rightwise]] man, shall give, and shall not cease.
21.27: The offerings of wicked men, that be offered of great trespass, be abominable.
21.28: A false witness shall perish; a man obedient shall speak victory.
21.29: A wicked man maketh firm his cheer unshamefastly; but he that is rightful [[or right]], amendeth his way.
21.30: No wisdom there is, no prudence there is, no counsel there is, against the Lord.
21.31: An horse is made ready to the day of battle; but the Lord shall give health.

22.1: Better is a good name, than many riches; for good grace is above silver and gold.
22.2: A rich man and a poor man met themselves; the Lord is [[the]] worker of ever either.
22.3: A fell man seeth evil, and hideth himself; and an innocent man passed, and he was tormented by harm.
22.4: The end of temperance is the dread of the Lord; riches, and glory, and life.
22.5: Armours [[or Arms]] and swords be in the way of a wayward man; but the keeper of his soul goeth away far from those [[or from them]].
22.6: It is a proverb, A young waxing man after his way, and when he hath waxed eld [[or eldeth]], he shall not go away from it.
22.7: A rich man commandeth to poor men; and he that taketh borrowing, is servant of the lender.
22.8: He that soweth wickedness shall reap evils; and the rod of his ire [[or his wrath]] shall be ended.
22.9: He that is ready to give mercy shall be blessed; for of his loaves he gave some to a poor man.
22.10: Cast thou out a scorner, and strife shall go out with him; and causes and despisings shall cease.
22.11: He that loveth the cleanness of heart, shall have the king for a friend, for the grace of his lips.
22.12: The eyes of the Lord keep knowing; and the words of a wicked man be deceived.
22.13: A slow man shall say, A lion is withoutforth; I shall be slain in the midst of the streets.
22.14: The mouth of an alien woman is a deep ditch; he to whom the Lord is wroth shall fall into it.
22.15: Folly is bound together in the heart of a child; and a rod of chastising [[or discipline]] shall drive it away.
22.16: He that falsely challengeth a poor man, to increase his own riches, shall give to a richer man, and he shall be needy.
22.17: My son, bow down thine ear, and hear thou the words of wise men; but set thou the heart to my teaching.
22.18: That shall be fair to thee, when thou hast kept it in thine heart, and it shall flow again in thy lips.
22.19: That thy trust be in the Lord; wherefore and I have showed it to thee today.
22.20: Lo! I have described it in three manners, in thoughts and knowing,
22.21: that I should show to thee the firmness and speeches of truth; to answer of these things to them that sent thee.
22.22: Do thou not violence to a poor man, for he is poor; neither defoul thou a needy man in the gate.
22.23: For the Lord shall deem his cause, and he shall torment them that tormented his soul.
22.24: Do not thou be friend to a wrathful man, neither go thou with a wrathful man;
22.25: lest peradventure thou learn his ways, and take cause of stumbling to thy soul.
22.26: Do not thou be with them that fasten, or bind, their hands, and that proffer themselves to be borrows for debts;
22.27: for if he hath not whereof he shall restore, what of cause is, that thou take away covering from thy bed?
22.28: Go thou not over the eld marks [[or the old terms]], or the boundary stones, which thy fathers have set.
22.29: Thou hast seen a man smart in his work; he shall stand before kings, and he shall not be before unnoble men.

23.1: When thou sittest to eat with the prince, perceive thou diligently what things be set before thy face,
23.2: and set thou a coulter in thy throat. If nevertheless thou hast power on thy soul,
23.3: desire thou not of his meats, in whom is the bread of lying.
23.4: Do not thou travail to be made rich, but set thou measure to thy prudence.
23.5: Raise not thine eyes to riches, which thou mayest not have; for those [[or they]] shall make to them-selves pens or wings, as of an eagle, and they shall fly into heaven.
23.6: Eat thou not with an envious man, and desire thou not his meats;
23.7: for at the likeness of a false diviner, and of a conjecturer, that is, expounder of dreams, he guesseth that, that he knoweth not. He shall say to thee, Eat thou and drink; and his soul is not with thee.
23.8: Thou shalt spew out the meat, which thou hast eaten; and thou shalt lose thy fair words.
23.9: Speak thou not in the ears of unwise men; for they shall despise the teaching of thy speech.
23.10: Touch thou not the terms, or the boundary stones, of little children; and enter thou not into the field of fatherless and motherless children.
23.11: For the neighbour of them is strong, and he shall deem their cause against thee.
23.12: Thine heart enter to teaching, and thine ears to the words of knowing.
23.13: Do not thou withdraw chastising or discipline, from a child; for though thou smitest him with a rod, he shall not die.
23.14: Thou shalt smite him with a rod, and thou shalt deliver his soul from hell.
23.15: My son, if thy soul is wise, mine heart shall have joy with thee;
23.16: and my reins shall make full out joy, when thy lips speak rightful [[or right]] things.
23.17: Thine heart pursue [[or follow]] not sinners; but be thou in the dread of the Lord all day.
23.18: For thou shalt have hope at the last, and thine abiding shall not be done away.
23.19: My son, hear thou, and be wise, and address thy soul in the way.
23.20: Do not thou be in the feasts of drinkers, neither in the oft eatings of them, that bring together fleshes to eat.
23.21: For men giving attention to drinks, and giving morsels together, shall be wasted, and napping shall be clothed with clothes rent.
23.22: Hear thy father, that begat thee; and despise not thy mother, when she is eld.
23.23: Buy thou truth, and do not thou sell wisdom, and doctrine, and understanding.
23.24: The father of a just [[or rightwise]] man joyeth full out with joy; he that begat a wise man, shall be glad in him.
23.25: Thy father and thy mother have joy, and he that begat thee, make full out joy.
23.26: My son, give thine heart to me, and thine eyes keep my ways.
23.27: For a whore is a deep ditch, and an alien woman, is a strait pit.
23.28: She setteth ambush in the way, as a thief; and shall add despisers in men, that is, shall multiply despisers of God among men.
23.29: To whom is woe? to whose father is woe? to whom be chidings? to whom be ditches? to whom be wounds without cause? to whom is putting out of eyes?
23.30: Whether not to them, that dwell in wine, and study to drink [[up]] all of cups?
23.31: Behold thou not [[the]] wine, when it sparkleth, when the colour thereof shineth in a glass cup. It entereth sweetly,
23.32: but at the last it shall bite as an adder, and as a cockatrice it shall shed abroad venoms.
23.33: Thine eyes shall see strange women, and thy heart shall speak wayward things.
23.34: And thou shalt be as a man sleeping in the midst of the sea, and as a governor asleeped [[or sleeping]], when the steering, either the instrument of governance, is lost.
23.35: And thou shalt say, They beat me, but I had not sorrow; they drew me, and I feeled not; when shall I wake out, and I shall find wines again?

24.1: Pursue [[or follow]] thou not evil men, desire thou not to be with them.
24.2: For the soul of them bethinketh on ravens, and their lips speak frauds.
24.3: An house shall be builded by wisdom, and it shall be made strong by prudence, or understanding.
24.4: [[The]] Cellars shall be filled in teaching, with all riches precious and full fair.
24.5: A wise man is strong, and a learned man is stalworth[[y]] and mighty.
24.6: For why battle is begun with ordinance; and health shall be, where many counsels be.
24.7: Wisdom is high to a fool; in the gate he shall not open his mouth.
24.8: He that thinketh to do evils, shall be called a fool.
24.9: The thought of a fool is sin; and a backbiter is abomination of men.
24.10: If thou hast slid, despairest in the day of anguish, thy strength shall be made less.
24.11: Deliver thou them, that be led to death; and cease thou not to deliver them, that be drawn to death.
24.12: If thou sayest, Strengths or Strong-holds suffice not; he that is [[the]] beholder of the heart, understandeth, and nothing deceiveth the keeper of thy soul, and he shall yield to a man after his works.
24.13: My son, eat thou honey, for it is good; and the honeycomb for it is full sweet to thy throat.
24.14: So and the teaching of wisdom is good to thy soul; and when thou hast found it, thou shalt have hope in the last things, and thine hope shall not perish.
24.15: Ambush thou not, and seek not wickedness in the house of a just [[or rightwise]] man, neither waste thou, his resting place.
24.16: For a just [[or rightwise]] man shall fall seven times in the day, and shall rise again; but wicked men shall fall into evil.
24.17: When thine enemy falleth, have thou not joy; and thine heart have not full out joying in his falling;
24.18: lest peradventure the Lord see, and it displease him, and he take away his ire [[or his wrath]] from him.
24.19: Strive thou not with the worst men, neither pursue [[or follow]] thou wicked men.
24.20: For why evil men have not hope of things to come, and the lantern of wicked men shall be quenched.
24.21: My son, dread thou God, and the king; and be thou not meddled [[or mingled]] with backbiters.
24.22: For their perdition shall rise together suddenly, and who knoweth the fall of ever either?
24.23: Also these things that pursue be to wise men. It is not good to know a person in doom.
24.24: Peoples shall curse them that say to a wicked man, Thou art just [[or rightwise]]; and lineages shall hold them abominable.
24.25: They that reprove justly sinners, shall be praised; and blessing shall come [[up]] on them.
24.26: He that answereth with rightful [[or right]] words, shall kiss lips.
24.27: Make ready thy work withoutforth, and work thy field diligently, that thou build thine house afterward.
24.28: Be thou not a witness without reasonable cause against thy neighbour; neither flatter thou any man with thy lips.
24.29: Say thou not, As he did to me, so I shall do to him, and I shall yield to each man after his work.
24.30: I passed by the field of a slow man, and by the vinery [[or the vineyard]] of a fond [[or foolish]] man;
24.31: and lo! nettles had filled all, thorns had covered the higher part thereof, and the wall of stones without mortar was destroyed.
24.32: And when I had seen this thing, I setted [[or put]] in mine heart, and by ensample, I learned teaching.
24.33: How long sleepest thou, slow man? when shalt thou rise from sleep? Soothly thou shalt sleep a little, thou shalt nap a little, thou shalt join together the hands a little, to take rest;
24.34: and then thy neediness as a courier shall come to thee, and thy beggary as an armed man.

25.1: Also these be the Parables of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah, translated.
25.2: The glory of God is to cover a word; and the glory of kings is to seek out a word.
25.3: Heaven above, and the earth beneath, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
25.4: Do thou away rust from silver, and a full clean vessel shall go out.
25.5: Do thou away unpiety from the cheer of the king, and his throne shall be made steadfast by rightfulness [[or rightwiseness]].
25.6: Appear thou not glorious before the king, and stand thou not in the place of great men.
25.7: For it is better, that it be said to thee, Ascend thou [[or Go up]] hither, than that thou be made low before the prince.
25.8: Bring thou not forth soon those things in strife, which thine eyes saw; lest afterward thou mayest not amend, when thou hast made thy friend unhonest or he hath shamed thee.
25.9: Treat thy cause with thy friend, and show thou not private matter to a strange man;
25.10: lest peradventure he have joy of thy fall, when he hath heard, and cease not to do shame to thee.
25.11: A golden pomme or pommel in beds of silver is he, that speaketh a word in his time.
25.12: A golden earring, and a shining pearl is he, that reproveth a wise man, and an ear obeying.
25.13: As the cold of snow in the day of harvest, so a faithful messenger to him that sent him, maketh his soul to have rest.
25.14: A cloud and wind, and rain not pursuing [[or following]], is a glorious man, and not [[ful]] filling promises.
25.15: A prince shall be made soft by patience; and a soft tongue shall break hardness.
25.16: Thou hast found honey, eat thou that that sufficeth to thee; lest per-adventure thou be [[full]]-filled, and spew it out.
25.17: Withdraw thy foot from the house of thy neighbour; lest sometime he be filled, that is, annoyed, and hate thee.
25.18: A dart, and a sword, and a sharp arrow, is a man that speaketh false witnessing against his neighbour.
25.19: A rotten tooth, and a faint foot is he, that hopeth on an unfaithful man in the day of anguish,
25.20: and loseth his mantle in the day of cold. Vinegar in a vessel of salt is he, that singeth songs to the worst heart. As a moth annoyeth or harmeth a cloth, and a worm a tree, so the sorrow of a man annoyeth the heart.
25.21: If thine enemy hungereth, feed thou him; if he thirsteth, give thou him water to drink;
25.22: for thou shalt gather together coals on his head; and the Lord shall yield to thee.
25.23: The north wind scattereth abroad rains; and a sorrowful face destroyeth a tongue backbiting.
25.24: It is better to sit in the corner of an house without [[a]] roof, than with a woman full of chiding, and in a common house.
25.25: Cold water to a thirsty man; and a good messenger from a far land.
25.26: A well disturbed with foot, and a vein broken, is a just [[or rightwise]] man falling before a wicked man.
25.27: As it is not good to him that eateth much honey; so he that is a searcher of majesty, shall be put down from glory.
25.28: As a city open, and without compass of walls; so is a man that may not refrain his spirit in speaking.

26.1: As snow in summer, and rain in harvest; so glory is unseemly to a fool.
26.2: For as a bird flying over to high things, and as a sparrow going into uncertain; so cursing brought forth without reasonable cause shall come above into some man.
26.3: Beating be to an horse, and a bridle to an ass; and a rod to the back of unprudent men.
26.4: Answer thou not to a fool after his folly, lest thou be made like him.
26.5: Answer thou a fool after his folly, lest he seem to himself to be wise.
26.6: An halting man in feet, and drinking wickedness, he that sendeth words by a fond [[or foolish]] messenger.
26.7: As an halting man hath fair legs in vain; so a parable is unseemly in the mouth of fools.
26.8: As he that sendeth a stone into the broad place of the sling; so he that giveth honour to an unwise man.
26.9: As if a thorn groweth in the hand of a drunken man; so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
26.10: Doom determineth causes; and he that setteth silence to a fool, assuageth ires [[or wraths]].
26.11: As a dog that turneth again to his spewing [[or As an hound that turneth again to his vomit]]; so is an unprudent man, that rehearseth his folly.
26.12: Thou hast seen a man seem wise to himself; an unknowing man shall have hope more than he.
26.13: A slow man saith, A lion is in the way, a lioness is in the footpaths.
26.14: As a door is turned in his hinges; so a slow man in his bed.
26.15: A slow man hideth his hands under his armpit; and he travaileth, if he turneth them up to his mouth.
26.16: A slow man seemeth wiser to himself, than seven men speaking sentences.
26.17: As he that taketh a dog by the ears; so he that passeth, and is unpatient, and is meddled [[or mingled]] with the chiding of another man.
26.18: As he is guilty, that sendeth spears and arrows into death,
26.19: so a man that annoyeth guilefully his friend, and when he is taken, he shall say, I did playing.
26.20: When trees [[or woods shall]] fail, the fire shall be quenched; and when a privy backbiter is withdrawn, strives rest.
26.21: As dead coals at [[or to]] quick coals, and trees at the fire [[or wood to fire]]; so a wrathful man raiseth chidings.
26.22: The words of a privy backbiter be as simple; and those [[or they]] come till to the innerest things of the heart.
26.23: As if thou wouldest adorn a vessel of earth with the dross of silver, so be swelling lips fellowshipped with a full wicked heart.
26.24: An enemy is understood by his lips, when he treateth guiles in his heart.
26.25: When he maketh low his voice, believe thou not to him; for seven wickednesses be in his heart.
26.26: The malice of him that covereth hatred guilefully, shall be showed in a council.
26.27: He that delveth a ditch, shall fall into it; and if a man walloweth a stone, it shall turn again to him.
26.28: A false tongue loveth not [[the]] truth; and a slippery mouth worketh fallings.

27.1: Have thou not glory of the morrow, that knowest not what thing the day coming shall bring forth.
27.2: Another man, and not thy mouth praise thee; a stranger, and not thy lips.
27.3: A stone is heavy, and gravel is chargeous; but the ire [[or the wrath]] of a fool is heavier than ever either.
27.4: Ire [[or Wrath]] hath no mercy, and strong vengeance breaking out hath no mercy; and who may suffer the fierceness of a spirit stirred?
27.5: Better is open reproving, than a love hid. [[Better is open amending, than hid love.]]
