27.6: Better be the wounds of him that loveth, than the guileful kisses of him that hateth.
27.7: A man [[ful]] filled shall despise an honeycomb; but an hungry man shall take, yea, bitter thing for sweet.
27.8: As a bird passing over from his nest, so is a man that forsaketh his place.
27.9: The heart delighteth in ointment, and diverse odours; and a soul is made sweet by the good counsels of a friend.
27.10: Forsake thou not thy friend, and the friend of thy father; and enter thou not into the house of thy brother, in the day of thy torment. Better is a neighbour nigh, than a brother afar.
27.11: My son, study thou about wisdom, and make thou glad mine heart; that thou mayest answer a word to a despiser.
27.12: A fell man seeing evil was hid; little men of wit passing forth suffered harms.
27.13: Take thou away his cloth, that promised for a stranger; and take thou away a wed from him for an alien man.
27.14: He that blesseth his neighbour with [[a]] great voice; and riseth by night, shall be like him that curseth.
27.15: Roofs dropping in the day of cold, and a woman full of chiding, be likened together.
27.16: He that withholdeth her, as if he holdeth [[or held the]] wind; and voideth [[out]] the oil of his right hand.
27.17: Iron is whetted by iron; and a man whetteth the face of his friend.
27.18: He that keepeth a fig tree, shall eat the fruits thereof; and he that is a keeper of his lord, shall be glorified.
27.19: As the cheers of men beholding themselves shine in waters; so the hearts of men be open to prudent men.
27.20: Hell and perdition shall not be filled; so and the eyes of men be not able to be filled [[or be unfillable]].
27.21: As silver is proved in a welling place, and gold is proved in a furnace; so a man is proved by the mouth of his praisers.
27.22: Though thou poundedest a fool in a mortar, as with a pestle smiting above dried barley, his folly shall not be done away from him.
27.23: Know thou diligently the cheer of thy beast; and behold thou thy flocks.
27.24: For thou shalt not have power continually; but a crown shall be given to thee in generation and into generation[[s]].
27.25: Meadows be opened, and green herbs appeared; and hay is gathered from [[the]] hills.
27.26: Lambs be to thy clothing; and kids be to the price of the field.
27.27: The milk of goats suffice to thee for thy meats; into the necessary things of thine house, and to lifelode of thine handmaidens.

28.1: A wicked man fleeth, when no man pursueth; but a just [[or rightwise]] man as a lion trusting shall be without fearedfulness.
28.2: For the sins of the land there be many princes of it; and for the wisdom of a man, and for the knowing of these things that be said, the life of the duke shall be the longer.
28.3: A poor man falsely challenging poor men, is like a great rain, wherein hunger is made ready.
28.4: They that forsake the law, praise the wicked man; they that keep the law, be kindled, or stirred [[up]], against him.
28.5: Wicked men think not on doom; but they that seek the Lord, perceive all things.
28.6: Better is a poor man going in his simpleness, than a rich man in [[his]] shrewd ways.
28.7: He that keepeth the law, is a wise son; but he that feedeth gluttons, shameth his father.
28.8: He that gathereth together riches by usuries, and free increases, gathereth those [[or them]] together against poor men.
28.9: His prayer shall be made cursed, that boweth away his ear, that he hear not the law.
28.10: He that deceiveth just [[or rightwise]] men in an evil way, shall fall in his perishing; and just [[or rightwise]] men shall wield his goods.
28.11: A rich man seemeth wise to himself; but a poor man prudent shall search him out or know his counsel.
28.12: In [[the]] enhancing of just [[or rightwise]] men is much glory; when wicked men reign, fallings of men be.
28.13: He that hideth his great trespasses, shall not be made rightful; but he that acknowledgeth and forsaketh them, shall get mercy.
28.14: Blessed is the man, which is ever dreadful; but he that is of hard heart, shall fall into evil.
28.15: A roaring lion, and an hungry bear, is a wicked prince on a poor people.
28.16: A duke needy of prudence shall oppress many men by false challenge; but the days of him that hateth avarice shall be made long.
28.17: No man sustain a man that falsely challengeth the blood of a man, if he fleeth till to the pit.
28.18: He that goeth simply shall be safe; he that goeth by wayward ways, shall fall down [[at]] once.
28.19: He that worketh his land, shall be filled with loaves; he that pursueth [[or followeth]] idleness, shall be filled with neediness.
28.20: A faithful man shall be praised much; but he that hasteth to be made rich, shall not be innocent.
28.21: He that knoweth a face in doom, doeth not well; this man forsaketh truth, yea, for a morsel of bread.
28.22: A man that hasteth to be made rich, and hath envy to other men, knoweth not that neediness shall come [[up]] on him.
28.23: He that reproveth a man, shall find grace afterward with him; more than he that deceiveth by flatterings of tongue.
28.24: He that withdraweth anything from his father and from his mother, and saith that this is no sin, is partner of a man-queller.
28.25: He that avaunteth himself, and alargeth, raiseth up strives; but he that hopeth in the Lord, shall be saved.
28.26: He that trusteth in his heart, is a fool; but he that goeth wisely, shall be praised.
28.27: He that giveth to a poor man, shall not be needy; he that despiseth a poor man beseeching, shall suffer neediness.
28.28: When unpious men rise, men shall be hid; and when they have perished, just [[or rightwise]] men shall be multiplied.

29.1: Sudden perishing shall come [[up]] on that man, that with hard noll, that is, an obstinate soul, despiseth a blamer; and health shall not follow him.
29.2: The commonality shall be glad in the multiplying of just [[or rightwise]] men; when wicked men have taken princehood, the people shall wail.
29.3: A man that loveth wisdom, maketh glad his father; but he that nourisheth a strumpet, shall lose his chattel [[or substance]].
29.4: A just king raiseth [[up]] the land; an avaricious man shall destroy it.
29.5: A man that speaketh by flattering and feigned words to his friend, spreadeth abroad a net to his steps.
29.6: A snare shall wrap a wicked man doing sin; and a just [[or rightwise]] man shall praise, and make joy.
29.7: A just [[or rightwise]] man knoweth the cause of poor men; and an unpious man knoweth not knowing.
29.8: Men full of pestilence destroy a city; but wise men turn away strong vengeance.
29.9: If a wise man striveth with a fool, whether he be wroth, or laugh, he shall not find rest.
29.10: Men-quellers hate a simple man; but just [[or rightwise]] men seek his soul.
29.11: A fool bringeth forth all his spirit; a wise man delayeth, and reserveth into time coming afterward.
29.12: A prince that heareth willfully the words of leasing, shall have all his servants unfaithful.
29.13: A poor man and a lender met themselves; the Lord is [[the]] lightener of ever either.
29.14: If a king deemeth poor men in truth, his throne shall be made steadfast [[into]] without end.
29.15: A rod and chastising [[or discipline]] shall give wisdom; but a child, that is left to his own will, shameth his mother.
29.16: Great trespasses shall be multiplied in the multiplying of wicked men; and just [[or rightwise]] men shall see the fallings of them.
29.17: Teach thy son, and he shall comfort thee; and he shall give delights to thy soul.
29.18: When prophecy faileth, the people shall be destroyed; but he that keepeth the law, is blessed.
29.19: A servant may not be taught by words; for he understandeth that that thou sayest, and he despiseth to answer.
29.20: Thou hast seen a man swift to speak; folly shall be hoped more than his amending [[or folly more is to be hoped for than the correction of him]].
29.21: He that nourisheth his servant delicately from childhood, shall find him a rebel [[or unobedient]] afterward.
29.22: A wrathful man stirreth chidings; and he that is light to have indignation, shall be more inclined to sins.
29.23: Lowness followeth a proud man; and glory shall up-take a meek man of spirit.
29.24: He that taketh part with a thief, hateth his soul; he heareth a man charging greatly, and showeth not.
29.25: He that dreadeth a man, shall fall soon; he that hopeth in the Lord, shall be raised [[up]].
29.26: Many men seek the face of the prince; and the doom of all men shall go forth of the Lord.
29.27: Just [[or Rightwise]] men have abomination of a wicked man; and wicked men have abomination of them, that be in a rightful [[or the right]] way.

30.1: The words of him that gathereth, of the son spewing. The prophecy which a man spake, with whom God was, and which man was comforted by God dwelling with him, and said,
30.2: I am the most foolish of men; and the wisdom of men is not with me.
30.3: I learned not wisdom; and I knew not the knowing of holy men.
30.4: Who ascended [[or went up]] into heaven, and came down? Who held together the spirit or wind in his hands? who bound together waters as in a cloth? Who raised up all the ends of [[the]] earth? What is the name of him? and what is the name of his son, if thou knowest?
30.5: Each word of God is a shield set afire, to all that hope in him.
30.6: Add thou not anything to the words of him, and thou be reproved, and be found a liar.
30.7: I prayed thee for two things; deny not thou them to me, before that I die.
30.8: Make thou far from me vanity and words of leasing; give thou not to me begging and riches; but give thou only necessaries to my lifelode;
30.9: lest peradventure I be full-filled, and be drawn to deny, and say, Who is the Lord? and lest I be compelled by neediness, and steal, and forswear the name of my God.
30.10: Accuse thou not a servant to his lord, lest peradventure he curse thee, and thou fall down.
30.11: A generation that curseth his father, and that blesseth not his mother.
30.12: A generation that seemeth clean to itself, and nevertheless is not washed from his filths.
30.13: A generation whose eyes be high, and the eyelids thereof be raised [[up]] into high things.
30.14: A generation that hath swords for teeth, and eateth with his cheek teeth; that it eat [[the]] needy men of [[the]] earth, and the poor-alls [[or the poor]] of men.
30.15: The water leach hath two daughters, saying, Bring, bring. Three things be unable to be filled, and the fourth, that saith never, It sufficeth;
30.16: hell; and the mouth of the womb; and the earth that is never filled with water; but fire that saith never, It sufficeth.
30.17: Crows of the strand [[or the streams]] peck out that eye, that scorneth the father, and that despiseth the child-bearing of his mother; and the young of an eagle eat that eye.
30.18: Three things be hard to me, and utterly I know not the fourth thing;
30.19: the way of an eagle in heaven; the way of a serpent on a stone; the way of a ship in the middle of the sea; and the way of a man in his young waxing age.
30.20: Such is the way of a woman adulteress, which eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I wrought not evil.
30.21: The earth is moved by three things, and by the fourth thing, which it may not sustain;
30.22: by a servant, when he reigneth; by a fool, when he is filled with meat;
30.23: by an hateful woman, when she is taken in matrimony; and by an handmaid, when she is heir of her lady.
30.24: Four [[things]] be the least things of [[the]] earth, and those be wiser than wise men;
30.25: ants, a feeble people, that make ready meat in harvest to themselves;
30.26: a hare, a people unmighty, that setteth his bed in a stone;
30.27: a locust hath no king, and all goeth out by companies;
30.28: a lizard enforceth or endeavoureth with hands, and dwelleth in the houses of kings.
30.29: Three things there be, that go well, and the fourth thing, that goeth richly, either by prosperity.
30.30: A lion, strongest of beasts, shall not dread, at the meeting of any man;
30.31: a cock, girded [[up]] the loins; and a ram, and a king, and none there is that shall against-stand him.
30.32: He that appeareth a fool, after that he is raised [[up]] on high; for if he had understood, he had set his hand on his mouth.
30.33: Forsooth he that thrusteth strongly teats, to draw out milk, thrusteth out butter; and he that smiteth greatly, draweth out blood; and he that stirreth ires, bringeth forth discords.

31.1: The words of Lemuel, the king; the vision by which his mother taught him.
31.2: What, my darling? what, the darling of my womb? what, the darling of my desires?
31.3: Give thou not thy chattel [[or thy substance]] to women, and thy riches to do away kings.
31.4: A! Lemuel, do not thou give wine to kings; for no privacy there is, where drunkenness reigneth.
31.5: Lest peradventure they drink, and forget dooms, and change the cause of the sons of a poor man.
31.6: Give ye cider to them that mourn, and wine to them that be of bitter soul.
31.7: Drink they, and forget they their neediness; and think they no more on their sorrow.
31.8: Open thy mouth for a dumb man, and open thy mouth for the causes of all sons that pass forth.
31.9: Deem thou that that is just, and deem thou a needy man and a poor man.
31.10: Who shall find a strong woman? the price of her is [[a]] far, and from the last [[or utmost]] ends.
31.11: The heart of her husband trusteth in her; and he shall not have need to robberies.
31.12: She shall yield to him good, and not evil, in all the days of her life.
31.13: She sought wool and flax; and wrought by the counsel of her hands.
31.14: She is made as the ship of a merchant, that beareth his bread from [[a]] far.
31.15: And she rose by night, and gave lifelode to her menials, and meats to her handmaidens.
31.16: She beheld a field, and bought it; of the fruit of her hands she planted a vinery [[or a vineyard]].
31.17: She girded her loins with strength, and made strong her arm.
31.18: She tasted, and saw, that her merchandise was good; her lantern shall not be quenched in the night.
31.19: She put her hands to the wharve, and her fingers took the spindle.
31.20: She opened her hand to the needy man, and stretched forth her hands to a poor man.
31.21: She shall not dread for her house of the colds of snow; for all her menials be clothed with double clothes.
31.22: She made to her a ray-cloth; bis, either white silk, and purple is the cloth[[ing]] of her.
31.23: Her husband is noble in the gates, when he sitteth with the senators of [[the]] earth.
31.24: She made linen cloth, and sold it; and gave a girdle to a merchant.
31.25: Strength and fairness is the clothing of her; and she shall laugh in the last day.
31.26: She opened her mouth to wisdom; and the law of mercy is in her tongue.
31.27: She beheld the paths of her house; and she ate not bread idly.
31.28: Her sons rose up, and preached her most blessed; her husband rose, and praised her.
31.29: Many daughters gathered riches; thou passedest them all.
31.30: Fairness is deceivable grace, and vain; that woman, that dreadeth the Lord, [[she]] shall be praised.
31.31: Give ye to her of the fruit of her hands; and her works praise her in the gates.
